credit_system.credit_hour: One semester credit hour for each 15 hours of classroom contact plus 30 hours of outside preparation (or 30 hours of lab/practica/studio work plus about 15 hours of preparation; or at least 45 hours of internship or shop instruction). The catalog notes that in most baccalaureate programs a student must earn at least 15 credits per semester to graduate in four years; a bachelor's degree requires a minimum of 120 credits.
credit_system.grading: Letter grades with quality points: A 4.0, A- 3.7, B+ 3.3, B 3.0, B- 2.7, C+ 2.3, C 2.0, C- 1.7, D+ 1.3, D 1.0, D- 0.7. Use of + or - is limited to A-, B+, B-, C+, C-, D+, and D-.
credit_system.math_placement: First math course is chosen from a math placement exam score (ALEKS placement test; M01/M02/M03 scores from the Maplesoft Math Placement Exams in Moodle) and the math track tied to the student's major; the student and advisor use the placement chart to select the course, and students are strongly encouraged to register at or below their placement level.

majors.name: Computer Science B.S. - Software Engineering
majors.description: Computer Science at UM is offered with concentrations in algorithm design, data science, mathematical sciences or software engineering; the program page notes that UM's computer science majors routinely receive paid internships at local and international tech firms. Required math: M 171 Calculus I or M 162 Applied Calculus, M 225 Introduction to Discrete Mathematics, plus one upper-division math elective (M 361, M 362, M 414, M 440, M 485 or STAT 421).
majors.career_outcomes: The program page lists jobs such as Computer Programmer, Software Engineer, Software Developer, Network Administrator, Computer Games Developer, Sensor Analyst, Web Developer, Researcher and Data Scientist.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take CSCI 150 Introduction to Computer Science in your first autumn semester to see if programming fits you, and check your math placement for M 171/M 162.

majors.name: Accounting B.S. in Business Administration
majors.accreditation: AACSB International (accounting programs hold separate AACSB accounting accreditation in addition to the College of Business AACSB accreditation)
majors.description: The undergraduate accounting program is committed to preparing students to apply accounting and business knowledge in organizations. Students develop competence in a broad range of accounting practices. Required math: one of M 115, M 121, M 151 or M 162, plus one statistics course (STAT 216 preferred).
majors.career_outcomes: The program page lists Certified Public Accountant, personal financial advisor, auditor, financial analyst, forensic accountant, environmental accountant and actuary; it states over 90% of graduates are employed in their field or accepted to graduate school within three months of graduation and 80% of students complete at least one internship.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take BGEN 105S Introduction to Business in your first autumn semester, then ACTG 201 Principles of Financial Accounting in sophomore autumn.

majors.name: Wildlife Biology B.S. - Terrestrial
majors.college: W.A. Franke College of Forestry and Conservation
majors.description: Wildlife Biology at the University of Montana has been training wildlife professionals since 1936; the terrestrial concentration focuses on birds and mammals and their habitats. The major requires a minimum GPA of 2.5. Required math: M 162 Applied Calculus or M 171 Calculus I, plus WILD 245 Wildlife Data, Inference, and Statistics.
majors.career_outcomes: The program page lists wildlife and/or fisheries biologist, wildlife conservation officer/game warden, wildlife/terrestrial program manager, wildlife researcher, and wildlife and/or fisheries technician.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take WILD 180 Careers in Wildlife Biology in your first autumn semester, alongside BIOB 160 and CHMY 121N.

majors.name: Psychology B.A.
majors.college: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
majors.description: Psychology at the University of Montana is one of the largest programs on campus. Students must complete a minimum of 60 credits in non-psychology courses. Required math: one of M 115, M 121, M 151, M 162 or M 171, plus PSYX 222 Psychological Statistics (or STAT 216).
majors.career_outcomes: The program page lists social worker, career counselor, human resources specialist, corrections officer, business/marketing/sales, real estate agent, preschool teacher, politics, business owner, statistician and advocacy; school psychologist, psychologist, mental health counselor and attorney require additional graduate training.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take PSYX 100S Intro to Psychology in your first autumn semester.

majors.name: Journalism B.A.
majors.college: College of the Arts and Media
majors.accreditation: Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC)
majors.description: The School of Journalism at the University of Montana is a nationally top-10 ranked, ACEJMC-accredited program. In the first three or four semesters of study, students take courses in the major and in the liberal arts and sciences. No math course is listed in the major requirements (only general education math applies).
majors.career_outcomes: The program page lists reporter, editor, freelance or magazine writer, news producer, broadcaster, podcaster, audio producer, TV anchor, video creator, social media strategist, PR specialist, film and video photographer/editor, and photographer.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take JRNL 100H Journalism and American Society in your first autumn semester, then JRNL 170 Writing the News in spring.
